transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

I’ve been seeing and hearing things at work and at home that no one else seems to notice, and it’s starting to scare me. It has gotten to the point where I don't know what is real anymore and I really need some help.
Can you tell me more about what you're seeing and hearing, and have you experienced any unusual beliefs or thoughts that others don't share?

I keep hearing my name whispered and a man's voice commenting on my work or warning me about "them," while also seeing shadowy figures in the doorway that vanish when I look straight at them. I've also been convinced that our office emails and calendar invites contain coded messages that my boss and coworkers are using to secretly coordinate against me to push me out, even though everyone else says it's just normal work stuff.
Have you experienced any periods where these voices, shadowy figures, or beliefs about coded messages stopped or significantly decreased for a while, only to return later?

No, they haven't really stopped or gone away; they've been pretty steady for about the last ten months. They definitely get much louder and more intense when I'm in one of my high-energy phases, but they still persist even during times when my mood feels completely flat or neutral.
Do you find that your thoughts are often disorganized, making it hard for you to express yourself or follow a conversation, especially when these voices or beliefs are most prominent?

Yes, especially during those times, my thoughts race so fast that I jump from one idea to the next, which often leaves people confused or cutting me off. I just feel this intense pressure in my chest to keep talking and explaining everything before the ideas slip away.

You mentioned having high-energy phases and times when your mood feels completely flat or neutral; can you tell me more about what happens during these high-energy phases, such as any changes in your sleep or activity level?

During those phases, I feel incredibly wired and only sleep a couple of hours a night, yet I wake up feeling completely charged. I'll stay up all night reorganizing files, starting spreadsheets, and rewriting policies, but I just bounce from task to task without finishing anything. My mood also swings wildly, going from feeling on top of the world to suddenly snapping at my wife and coworkers over tiny things.

Do you think these high-energy phases and the accompanying mood swings, disorganized thoughts, and increased intensity of the voices and beliefs are part of the same problem, or do they seem like separate issues to you?

They definitely feel connected to me. When I'm in those high-energy phases and barely sleeping, that's exactly when the whispers get the loudest and the shadowy figures show up the most. It feels like the intense energy and those strange experiences are happening at the exact same time.
Can you describe how long these high-energy phases typically last and whether you've noticed any pattern or triggers that lead into or out of these phases?

These high-energy phases have been going on for almost this entire past year with only brief breaks, so I feel revved up most of the time. The major trigger that started all of this was my company's reorganization fifteen months ago, which completely disrupted my routines. Otherwise, I don't really notice any specific day-to-day triggers that switch me in or out of them; they just seem to happen.

Do you experience significant depressive episodes where you feel extremely low in mood, loss of interest in activities, and decreased energy, which could last for days or weeks, separate from your described high-energy phases?

Yes, outside of the high-energy spells, I have days where I just sit at my computer feeling completely flat and blank, ignoring friends and skipping my art group and hiking because I can't bring myself to care. These drained, low periods definitely happen, but looking back over the year, I've spent much more of my time in those revved-up, high-energy phases than in these flat ones.

Can you estimate how many days out of the year you've spent in these high-energy phases versus the number of days spent in the low, flat periods, and do you think the high-energy phases have ever led to significant problems in your relationships, work, or daily life?

I've spent the vast majority of the past year—easily most of the days—in those high-energy, revved-up phases rather than the flat, low ones. It has caused massive problems, from me snapping at my wife and coworkers to missing deadlines and having projects taken away, to the point where my wife had to step in with HR because I couldn't manage my responsibilities anymore.

Can you clarify whether the periods of feeling completely flat or neutral, which you described as happening outside of your high-energy phases, have ever lasted for two weeks or more at a time, and if so, how they compare in duration to your high-energy phases?

Yes, earlier this year I had a stretch of a few weeks where my mood felt completely neutral, neither high nor low, though I was still hearing the whispers and believing the emails were coded. But looking back over the whole year, those neutral or flat times were pretty brief compared to the high-energy phases, which have taken up the vast majority of my time.

Can you confirm whether the periods of feeling completely flat or neutral, which seemed to last for a few weeks, met the full criteria for a major depressive episode, including significant loss of interest in activities, changes in appetite or sleep, fatigue, feelings of worthlessness, or recurrent thoughts of death?

During those weeks, my mood felt more flat and neutral rather than deeply depressed, though I did completely lose interest in hiking and my art group and had no motivation to do anything. I didn't experience feelings of worthlessness, changes in my appetite, or thoughts of death; it was just an empty state where I sat at my computer unable to care.

Have you ever had a distinct period of at least two weeks where you felt persistently depressed, with either depressed mood most of the day or markedly diminished interest or pleasure in activities, and at least five other specific depressive symptoms were present, such as significant weight loss or gain, insomnia or hypersomnia, fatigue, feelings of worthlessness, or diminished ability to think?

I do experience times where I feel completely flat and blank, just staring at my computer and losing all interest in my art group or hiking. However, I don't have those other symptoms you mentioned, like feelings of worthlessness or major changes in my weight. It really feels more like an empty, unmotivated state rather than a deep, painful depression.
Can you describe if there has ever been a period where you experienced both the high-energy phases and the flat, depressed-like periods simultaneously, or do they always seem to occur separately?

They definitely occur separately rather than at the same time. Outside of those high-energy, revved-up spells where I'm pacing and full of ideas, I have these separate, flatter periods. During those times, I feel completely drained and just sit staring at my computer, without the energy to care about anything.

Have you ever experienced a period of at least two weeks where you felt persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable, with at least three other specific symptoms such as inflated self-esteem, decreased need for sleep, more talkative than usual, flight of ideas, distractibility, increase in goal-directed activity, or excessive involvement in pleasurable activities that have a high potential for painful consequences?

Yes, I've absolutely experienced those phases for much longer than two weeks; they've actually been happening for almost this entire past year with only brief breaks. During these times, I either feel on top of the world or extremely irritable and quick to snap, sleeping only a couple of hours a night but waking up fully charged. I'll pace around starting unfinished spreadsheets or policy rewrites, talking so rapidly that others get confused, and honestly believing I have a special ability to decode the company's communications.

Can you clarify if the flat periods you've described have ever met the full criteria for a major depressive episode, lasting at least two weeks with significant symptoms, or if they've always been more brief and less severe?

No, I don't think those flat periods have ever reached the level of a full clinical depression. They feel more like being completely blank, empty, and lacking the motivation to do things like my art or see friends, rather than feeling intense sadness. These drained phases are also much shorter and happen far less often than my high-energy periods.
Do you think the voices, shadowy figures, and beliefs about coded messages are more prominent or intense during your high-energy phases, or are they separate from your mood swings and energy levels?

It's actually a bit of both; during my highly energized, sleepless periods, the whispers get loudest and the shadowy figures show up the most, so they definitely feel connected. However, they aren't entirely dependent on those highs, because during a neutral stretch earlier this year, I was still hearing my name whispered and remained convinced that the company emails were coded messages about me.

Can you tell me if the voices, shadowy figures, and beliefs about coded messages ever completely disappear during your brief, flat periods, or do they persist at some level even when your mood and energy are more neutral?

No, they don't completely disappear, which is really exhausting. Even during that neutral stretch earlier this year when my energy was flat and I didn't feel high or low, I still heard the whispers and was convinced the emails were coded messages about me. It's like those experiences are always there in the background, no matter how my mood shifts.

Have you ever experienced a period where the voices, shadowy figures, or beliefs about coded messages stopped or significantly decreased when your mood was stable and you weren't in a high-energy phase, or have these symptoms persisted regardless of your mood state?

No, they didn't stop during that time. Earlier this year, when my mood felt completely neutral and stable without any highs or crashes, I still heard my name whispered and remained convinced that the emails were coded messages about me. Those experiences seem to persist regardless of whether my mood is up or down.

Have you ever experienced a period where the voices, shadowy figures, and beliefs about coded messages were completely absent for at least a month, or have they been consistently present throughout the past year?

No, they haven't been absent at all. For roughly the past ten months, the whispers, the shadowy figures, and my beliefs about the emails have been pretty steady and constant. I haven't had any long breaks or periods where they completely disappeared.

When you're experiencing your high-energy phases, do the voices and shadowy figures seem to be directly related to your mood, such as commenting on your elevated mood or energy, or do they seem unrelated to your mood state?

The voices don't actually comment on my high mood or energy; instead, the man's voice comments on my work or warns me about "them" coordinating against me. However, they are definitely tied to my energy levels in terms of timing, getting the loudest and most frequent during my super-charged phases. They aren't completely dependent on my mood though, because I still experienced the whispers and shadowy figures during that neutral stretch earlier this year when my energy was flat.

Do you think the voices and shadowy figures are more closely tied to your mood swings, or do they seem to be a separate issue that happens regardless of whether you're in a high-energy phase or a flat period?

It feels like a mix of both, because during my high-energy phases, the whispers get much louder and the shadowy figures show up more often. However, they also happen completely independent of my mood, like during that neutral stretch earlier this year when I still heard the voices and believed the emails were coded.

Do you think the voices, shadowy figures, and beliefs about coded messages are ever triggered by or closely follow your shifts in mood and energy, or do they seem to occur independently of your mood swings?

It's really a mix of both, because during my high-energy, super-charged phases, the whispers definitely get loudest and the shadowy figures show up most frequently. However, they also occur independently of my mood, like earlier this year when my mood felt completely neutral but I still heard the whispers and believed the emails were coded.

Do you think the voices, shadowy figures, and coded message beliefs would still be present if you weren't experiencing these high-energy phases and mood swings, or are they closely tied to your overall mood state?

Yes, I definitely think they would still be there because they don't only happen when my mood is swinging. Earlier this year, I had a stretch of a few weeks where my mood was completely flat and neutral, with no highs or crashes at all. Yet, even during that stable time, I was still hearing the whispers and was convinced the emails were coded messages about me.
Have you ever experienced a period where you had no hallucinations or delusional thoughts for at least a month, or have these symptoms been consistently present throughout the past year?

No, they have been consistently present without any real breaks. For about the last ten months, the whispers, shadowy figures, and my beliefs about the coded emails have been happening pretty steadily. I definitely haven't had a month-long period where they completely disappeared.

Have you ever experienced a period where your hallucinations or delusional thoughts were directly influenced or triggered by your mood swings, such as becoming more intense during manic phases or less prominent during depressive phases?

Yes, they definitely intensify during my high-energy phases; when I'm barely sleeping and racing around with big plans, the whispers get the loudest and the shadowy figures appear the most. However, they aren't completely triggered by my mood, since I still experienced the whispers and the belief about coded emails during that neutral stretch earlier this year when my energy was completely flat.
Do you think your hallucinations and delusional thoughts are a direct result of your mood swings, or do they seem to be separate issues that happen regardless of your mood state?

It feels like both, because during my high-energy phases, the whispers get much louder and the shadowy figures appear more frequently, making them seem linked to my mood. However, they also happen independently, like during a neutral stretch earlier this year when my mood was completely stable but I still heard the whispers and believed the emails were coded messages for a couple of weeks.

Can you describe any periods where your hallucinations or delusional thoughts changed or disappeared when you were not experiencing any mood swings or high-energy phases, and if so, how long these periods lasted?

They didn't actually disappear or change at all during those times. Earlier this year, I had a stretch of a couple of weeks where my mood felt completely neutral with no highs or crashes, but the whispers and the belief about the coded emails continued steadily. Even though I wasn't feeling buzzed or manic, those strange experiences didn't fade.

Can you clarify if the intensity or presence of the whispers, shadowy figures, and beliefs about coded messages ever completely normalize or disappear for an extended period when you're not in a high-energy phase or experiencing significant mood swings?

No, they never completely disappear or normalize, even during those quiet times. For example, earlier this year when my mood was completely neutral and I had no racing energy, I still heard my name whispered and believed the emails were coded messages. Those experiences just seem to persist regardless of whether I'm having mood swings.

Do you think the voices and shadowy figures are directly related to your mood, such as being worse when you're manic or better when you're depressed, or do they seem to be separate from your mood swings?

It's really both. During my high-energy, super-charged phases, the whispers get the loudest and the shadowy figures show up the most. But they also happen completely on their own, like earlier this year when my mood was totally neutral for a few weeks but I still heard the voices and believed the emails were coded.
Do you think the voices, shadowy figures, and beliefs about coded messages would completely resolve if your mood swings and high-energy phases were treated and stabilized?

No, I don't think treating the mood swings would completely stop them. Earlier this year, there was a period when my mood felt totally neutral and I wasn't experiencing those high-energy phases, yet I was still hearing the whispers and felt convinced the company emails were coded messages about me.
